studies.title: Geroprotective effect of ala-glu-asp-gly peptide in male rats exposed to different illumination regimens.
studies.abstract: Exposure of male rats to permanent or natural illumination of North-Western Russia accelerated their death in comparison with animals exposed to standard (12 h) light. Permanent illumination promoted the development of spontaneous tumors in comparison with the standard photoregimen. Injection of epithalone (synthetic Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly peptide; subcutaneously 0.1 microg/rat 5 times a week from the age of 4 months until natural death) virtually did not change the mean lifespan of male rats, but was associated with a significant (p<0.05) normalization of population aging rate and hence, time of mortality rate doubling in groups exposed to natural or constant illumination. Epithalone injected to rats exposed to any photoregimen significantly inhibited the development of spontaneous tumors, primarily testicular leydigomas and leukemias.
studies.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine

studies.title: Effect of Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly peptide on life span and development of spontaneous tumors in female rats exposed to different illumination regimes.
studies.abstract: The effects of Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly peptide (Epithalon) on the life span and development of spontaneous tumors were studied in female rats exposed to standard, natural for North-Western Russia, and constant illumination. The mean life span of animals exposed to constant or natural illumination decreased by 13.5 and 25.5%, the maximum by 9 and 7 months, respectively, and spontaneous tumors developed much more rapidly than in animals living under conditions of the standard light regimen. Epithalon (0.1 microg daily 5 times a week from the age of 4 months) did not change the life span of rats living under conditions of standard day/night regimen, while in rats exposed to the natural and constant light it promoted prolongation of the maximum life span by 95 and 24 days, respectively. Epithalon prolonged the mean life span of the last 10% of rats exposed to natural and constant illumination, treated with Epithalon, by 137 and 43 days, respectively. This peptide exhibited virtually no effect on the development of spontaneous tumors in rats exposed to standard and constant illumination, but significantly inhibited their development in rats exposed to natural light.
studies.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine

studies.title: Effect of the synthetic pineal peptide epitalon on spontaneous carcinogenesis in female C3H/He mice.
studies.abstract: The potential preventive effect of the synthetic pineal peptide Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) on spontaneous tumorigenesis in mice was studied. One-year-old female C3H/He mice were kept for 6.5 months under standard conditions. Epitalon was injected at a dose of 0.1 microg, 5 times a week. Long-term exposure to Epitalon in small doses did not show any toxic effect. Treatment with Epitalon decreased the number of tumor-bearing mice with malignant tumors and prevented the development of metastases. Spontaneous tumors of the reproductive organs (mammary glands and ovaries) were predominant in both groups of mice (control and experimental). The mammary gland tumors were different variants of invasive ductal carcinomas. In the ovaries, granulosa-cell tumors were found. Tumors were in the minority in other organs and had benign characteristics. In control mice, metastases were found in 3 out of 9 tumor-bearing mice, all of them being from tumors of the reproductive organs. Treatment with Epitalon slowed down the development of metastases from spontaneous tumors, and no metastases were found in the experimental mice. These data highlight the antimetastatic effect of Epitalon as part of its oncostatic properties.

studies.title: [Effect of epitalon and melatonin on life span and spontaneous carcinogenesis in senescence accelerated mice (SAM)].
studies.abstract: Female senescence accelerated mice SAMP-1. (prone) and SAMR-1 (resistant) were exposed 5 times a week monthly to melatonin (with drinking water 20mg/ml during the night hours) or to s.c. injections of epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) at a single dose 1mkg/mouse. Control mice were intact or exposed to injection of 0.1 ml normal saline. The body weight and temperature, food consumption, estrous function were monitored regularly. The life span and tumor incidence were evaluated as well. As age advanced, the weight increased whereas food consumption and body temperature did not change. There was no significant substrain difference in these parameters. Exposure to melatonin or epitalon also failed to influence those indices. As age advanced, the incidence of irregular estrous cycles increased both in SAMP-1 and SAMR-1, whereas the treatment with both melatonin and epitalon prevented such disturbances. SAMP-1 revealed some features of accelerated aging as compared to SAMR-1. The mean life span of the 10% of the last survivors among treated SAMP-1 was shorter than that of SAMR-1, aging rate increased and mortality doubling time decreased. There was a direct correlation between body mass of the two substrains at the age of 3 and 12 months matched by body mass increase and longer life span. Melatonin or epitalon treatment was followed by longer mean and maximum survival in the 10% of the last survivors among SAMP-1. Melatonin involved decreased aging rate and increased mortality doubling time. Malignant lymphomas predominated in SAM without any significant difference in frequency between the substrains. While melatonin failed to influence tumor incidence or term of detection in SAMP-1, neither did epitalon affect frequency. However, it was followed by longer survival in tumor-free animals. No link between melatonin or epitalon treatment, on the one hand, and carcinogenesis, on the other, was reported in SAMR-1.

studies.title: Epitalon and colon carcinogenesis in rats: proliferative activity and apoptosis in colon tumors and mucosa.
studies.abstract: The effect of the synthetic pineal peptide Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) on proliferative activity in colon tumors, and in mucosal epithelial cells adjacent to and located far from tumors was studied in rats. To evaluate the effect of Epitalon on different stages of carcinogenesis, different treatment regimens were used: during the tumor initiation stage, during the tumor-promotion stage, or during the entire process of tumor development. Eighty 2-month-old male LIO rats were exposed weekly to five subcutaneous injections of 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) at a single dose of 21 mg/kg body weight. Rats were divided into four groups. Control rats (group 1) received saline at a dose of 0.1 ml during the entire experiment. Rats in group 2 were treated with Epitalon at a dose of 1 micro g, five times a week, for 6 months, from the first injection of DMH till the end of the experiment. Rats in group 3 were treated with Epitalon after termination of the carcinogen injections. Rats in group 4 were treated with Epitalon only during the period of DMH exposure (for the first 5 weeks of the experiment). DMH induced proliferation of the secretory epithelium, and this phenomenon was accompanied by a decrease in the size of the stromal area and the area of lymph infiltration in colon tumors and in the colon mucosa adjacent to the tumors (group 1). Epitalon attenuated this effect, especially when the treatment was continued throughout the experiment (group 2). It increased the stromal areas, as well as that of lymphoid infiltration in the colon mucosa adjacent to the tumors. The intensity of lymphoid infiltration was activated in both the colon mucosa adjacent to a tumor and in the tumor. Mitotic activity of tumor cells was significantly inhibited by Epitalon when the treatment was given throughout the experiment (group 2). In parallel, a high level of apoptosis was seen in the same group. Thus, the strongest inhibitory effect of Epitalon on carcinogenesis in the colon mucosa was manifested when the treatment was continued throughout the experiment.

studies.title: Effect of Epitalon on biomarkers of aging, life span and spontaneous tumor incidence in female Swiss-derived SHR mice.
studies.abstract: From the age of 3 months until their natural deaths, female outbred Swiss-derived SHR mice were subcutaneously injected on 5 consecutive days every month with 0.1 ml of normal saline (control) or with 1.0 microg/mouse (approximately 30-40 microg/kg) of tetrapeptide Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) dissolved in 0.1 ml saline. There were 54 mice in each group. The results of this study show that treatment with Epitalon did not influence food consumption, body weight or mean life span of mice. However, it slowed down the age-related switching-off of estrous function and decreased the frequency of chromosome aberrations in bone marrow cells (by 17.1%, P<0.05). It also increased by 13.3% the life span of the last 10% of the survivors (P<0.01) and by 12.3% the maximum life span in comparison with the control group. We also found that treatment with Epitalon did not influence total spontaneous tumor incidence, but inhibited the development of leukemia (6.0-fold), as compared with the control group. The data obtained suggest a geroprotector activity of Epitalon and the safety of its long-term administration in mice.

studies.title: Inhibitory effect of the peptide epitalon on the development of spontaneous mammary tumors in HER-2/neu transgenic mice.
studies.abstract: Female FVB/N HER-2/neu transgenic mice from the age of 2 months were subcutaneously injected with saline, the peptide Epitalon(R) (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) or with the peptide Vilon(R) (Lys-Glu) in a single dose of 1 microg/mouse for 5 consecutive days every month. Epitalon treatment reduced the cumulative number and the maximum size of tumors (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the number of mice bearing 1 mammary tumor was increased, whereas the number of mice bearing 2 or more mammary tumors was reduced in Epitalon-treated in comparison to saline-treated animals (p < 0.05). The size but not the number of lung metastases was reduced in Epitalon-treated compared to saline-treated mice (p < 0.05). The treatment with Vilon produced significant negative effects when compared to the control group, with an increased incidence of mammary cancer development (p < 0.05), a shorter mean latent period of tumors (p < 0.05) and an increased cumulative number of tumors (p < 0.05). A 3.7-fold reduction in the expression of HER-2/neu mRNA was found in mammary tumors from HER-2/neu transgenic mice treated with Epitalon compared to control animals. The expression of mRNA for HER-2/neu was also partially reduced in Vilon-treated mice, but it remained significantly higher in Vilon- than in Epitalon-treated animals (1.9-fold increase). The data demonstrate the inhibitory effect of Epitalon in the development of spontaneous mammary tumors in HER-2/neu mice, suggesting that a downregulation of HER-2/neu gene expression in mammary adenocarcinoma may be responsible, at least in part, for the antitumor effect of the peptide.

studies.title: Epithalon decelerates aging and suppresses development of breast adenocarcinomas in transgenic her-2/neu mice.
studies.abstract: Female transgenic FVB/N mice carrying the breast cancer gene HER-2/neu received epithalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) in a dose of 1 mg subcutaneously 5 times a week to from the 2nd month of life to death. Epithalon prolonged the average and maximum lifetimes of mice by 13.5 (p<0.05) and 13.9%, respectively. The peptide prolonged the average lifetime of animals without neoplasms (by 34.2%, p<0.05). Epithalon decelerated the development of age-related disturbances in reproductive activity and suppressed the formation of neoplasms. The peptide decreased the incidence of breast adenocarcinomas, lungs metastases (by 1.6 times, p<0.05), and multiple tumors (by 2 times). Epithalon 3.7-fold increased the number of mice without breast tumors (p<0.05), while the number of animals with 6 or more breast tumors decreased by 3 times (p<0.05). Epithalon prolonged the lifetime of mice with breast tumors by 1.4 times (p<0.05). These results indicate that Epithalon possesses geroprotective activity and inhibits breast carcinogenesis in transgenic mice, which is probably related to suppression of HER-2/neu expression.
studies.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine

studies.title: Inhibitory effect of peptide Epitalon on colon carcinogenesis induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine in rats.
studies.abstract: The effect of synthetic pineal peptide Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) on colon carcinogenesis was firstly studied in rats. Eighty 2-month-old outbred male LIO rats were subdivided into four groups and were weekly exposed to five subcutaneous injections of 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) at a single dose of 21 mg/kg body weight. Additionally, 5 days a week, some of the rats were given subcutaneous injections of saline at a dose of 0.1 ml during the whole experiment (group 1, control) or Epitalon at a single dose of 1 microg during the whole experiment (group 2), Epitalon after termination of carcinogen injections (group 3) or during the period of DMH exposure (group 4). Colon carcinomas developed in 90-100% of DMH-treated rats. The number of total colon tumors per rat was 4.1; 2.7; 3.7; 2.9 in groups 1, 2, 3, 4, respectively (the difference in groups 2 and 4 compared with group 1 is significant). In rats from group 2, colon tumors were smaller than in control animals. In group 2, the incidence, as well the multiplicity of tumors in ascending and descending colon, were significantly decreased in comparison with group 1. In group 4, the mean number of tumors per rat was significantly decreased, too. A trend to decrease the number of tumors in the rectum in rats from groups 2, 3 and 4, treated with Epitalon was found. Epitalon inhibited also the development of tumors in jejunum and ileum. Thus, our results demonstrated an inhibitory effect of Epitalon on chemically induced bowel carcinogenesis in rats.

studies.title: [Effect of Epitalon and Vilon treatment on mammary carcinogenesis in transgenic erbB-2/NEU mice].
studies.abstract: Female transgenic FVB mice transfected with the mammary erbB-2/neu oncogene were injected 0.1 ml 0.9% solution of sodium chloride (control), 1 meg Vilon peptide (Lys-Glu) or Epitalon peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Glu), s.c., 5 days in succession once a month, beginning from the age of 2 months. The characteristics of mammary tumor induction in the control and experimental groups did not differ until the age of 9 months. Later on, Epitalon-treated mice revealed distinct inhibition of carcinogenesis. One tumor per animal was detected in 7% (control), 4% (Vilon) and 16% (Epitalon) (p < 0.05). Two or more tumors per animal were in 75%, 95% and 56%, respectively (p < 0.05). Largest diameter of mammary adenocarcinoma in the Epitalon group was smaller than in controls by 33% (p < 0.05). Although the number of mice with metastases to the lung in all three groups was practically identical, their incidence in the Vilon group was 2.6 times higher than in Epitalon-treated animals (p < 0.05). Largest diameter of metastasis in the Epitalon group was the smallest, too. Our data point to inhibition of mammary carcinogenesis by Epitalon in transgenic erbB-2/neu mice.

studies.title: [Effect of vilon and epithalone on induction and growth of induced bladder neoplasms in rats].
studies.abstract: Experimental data on the effect of peptides--Vilon (Lys-Glu) and Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly)--on induction of urinary bladder tumors in rats are presented. Treatment with Vilon was followed by a significant fall in tumor incidence in 56% of experimental animals, as compared with 75.5% in control, as well as inhibition of early-onset neoplastic changes in the bladder mucosa. No inhibitory effect of Epitalon was recorded.

studies.title: [Effect of epithalone on growth kinetics and functional morphology of M-1 sarcoma].
studies.abstract: The growth of subcutaneously-transplanted sarcoma M-1 in rat was inhibited by injection of a synthetic tetrapeptide--epitalon (2.5 (micrograms/kg). The effect lasted for two weeks after injection course. Decrease in proliferative activity was not associated with the drug's immediate cytostatic action on tumor cells. The specific mechanism of the drug's action via blood flow was shown by morphological signs of hemorrhagic necrosis of tumor and increased apoptosis of tumor cells.

studies.title: Pineal-regulating tetrapeptide epitalon improves eye retina condition in retinitis pigmentosa.
studies.abstract: We have studied the effect of tetrapeptide Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) on the course of congenital pigmented degeneration of the retina. The application of Epitalon in Campbell rats is found to intensify the bioelectric and functional activity of the retina due to the preservation of its morphological structure. Epitalon therapy in patients with degenerative retinal lesions results in a positive clinical effect in 90% of the cases. The analysis of Epitalon effects suggests that the tetrapeptide participates in the mechanisms of transcription common for the epiphysis and retina.

studies.title: Retinoprotective effect of Epithalon in campbell rats of various ages.
studies.abstract: We studied the retinoprotective effect of Epithalon administered to the offspring of Campbell rats during postnatal ontogeny and to mothers before mating and during pregnancy. After this treatment the morphological structure and functional activity of the retina were preserved for a longer period compared to control rats (by 2 times) and to the animals receiving the peptide only during postnatal ontogeny (by 30%).
studies.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine

studies.title: [Aging of the pineal gland].
studies.abstract: The age-related changes in the pineal gland are functional rather than organic, which makes their correction or prevention more tenable. The amelioration or inhibition of some age-related impairments of the pineal gland were observed with dietary restriction and the use of S-adenosylmethionine or MAO-A inhibitors. A threefold increase in nocturnal melatonin peaks occurs in old rhesus monkeys treated with a synthetic peptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly (Epithalon) designed basing on the amino acid content of a pineal peptide extract Epithalamin. Other effects of Epithalon markedly overlap with melatonin effects. Besides life extension in mice and fruit flies, Epithalon effects include the postponing vision loss in Campbell rats with hereditary pigmental dystrophy. A uniting aspect of such a range of activities might be the participation of transcription factors, since they are often highly conservative in evolution and, on the other hand, may be strictly tissue-specific. The targets of Epithalon may include transfactors that in mammals are specific for the pineal gland and retina and exhibit impaired functions in the aged pineal gland.

studies.title: Effect of epithalon on age-specific changes in the retina in rats with hereditary pigmentary dystrophy.
studies.abstract: The effect of peptide bioregulator Epithalon on the course of hereditary pigmentary retinal degeneration was studied in Campbell rats. Administration of epithalon starting from birth protected morphological structure, increased its bioelectrical activity, and improved its function.

studies.title: Pineal peptides restore the age-related disturbances in hormonal functions of the pineal gland and the pancreas.
studies.abstract: The purpose of this research was to study age-related changes in functioning of pineal and pancreatic glands of non-human primates, rhesus monkeys, and to elucidate the possibility of their corrections with the help of epitalon, a synthetic analogue of the pharmacopoeia drug epithalamin. In old (20-27 years) animals, the basal plasma levels of glucose and insulin were found to be higher, while the night melatonin level was lower in comparison with (6-8 years) young animals. After the glucose administration to old monkeys, a larger area under the curve of the plasma glucose response, a reduced glucose 'disappearance' rate, and a reduced insulin peak (5 min after the glucose administration) were observed in comparison with young animals in similar experiments. The epitalon administration to old monkeys caused the decrease in the basal levels of glucose and insulin and the increase in the basal night melatonin level. Additionally, in the case of old monkeys, epitalon decreased the area under the plasma glucose response curve, markedly increased the glucose 'disappearance' rate and normalized the plasma insulin dynamics in response to glucose administration. Yet, it has not affected the hormonal and metabolic changes in young animals. Thus, epitalon is a promising factor for restoring the age-related endocrine dysfunctions of primates.

studies.title: Peptide correction of age-related hormonal dysfunction of the pancreas in monkeys.
studies.abstract: We studied the effect of Epithalon on the function of pancreatic islets and regulation of blood glucose level in female rhesus monkeys of various ages. Epithalon corrected the age-related decrease in glucose tolerance and restored the dynamics of insulin level in response to glucose load.

studies.title: [Effects of epithalon and cortagene on immunity and hemostasis in neonatally hypophysectomized chicken and old birds].
studies.abstract: It has been found that chicken hypophysectomized early in the neonatal period develop anemia, cellular and humoral immune deficiency, hypercoagulation and inhibited fibrinolysis by their 45th postnatal day. An analogous operation performed on old birds produces less significant changes in erythrocytes, immunity and hemostasis. Injections of epithalon tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) administered to either hypophysectomized chicken or old birds during a period of 40 days completely eliminate the shifts registered in erythrocytes, immunity and hemostasis, while injections of cortagene (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) which is distinguished from epithalon by a different terminal aminoacid (with Gly being replaced by Pro) do not affect the parameters studied.

studies.title: [Effect of epitalon on the immunity and hemostasis in hypophysectomized chicken and old hens].
studies.abstract: Neonatal hypophysectomy in chicken, as well as that in old hen has been established to entail in 1,5 months after surgery cellular and humoral immunity disturbances, pronounced hypercoagulation and fibrinolysis depression. Administration of Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) to a large extent eliminates revealed shifts. This effect appeared to be stronger in neonatally hypophysectomized chicken than in old hens.

studies.title: Effect of epitalon on interleukin-1beta signal transduction and the reaction of thymocyte blast transformation under stress.
studies.abstract: The aim of this research consisted in studying the effects of tetrapeptide Epitalon on both thymocyte proliferation and interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) signal transduction via sphingomyelin pathway in the cerebral cortex membranes of mice exposed to stresses exerting diverse effects upon humoral immune response. The experiments were performed on male (CBAxC(57)BL(6))F1 mice aged 8 10 weeks. Two models of experimental stress were used: immune-stimulatory rotation stress and immune-suppressive combined stress (cooling followed by immobilization). The concomitant effect of Epitalon was determined according to its influence on thymocyte proliferation stimulated by concanavalin A at a sub-optimal dose and recombinant IL-1beta. The activity of membrane neutral sphingomyelinase (nSMase), the key enzyme of the sphingomyelin signal transduction pathway, was assayed according to modified Rao and Spence's method (1976). The investigation demonstrated that Epitalon increased thymocyte proliferative activity, both enhanced under rotation stress and suppressed under combined one. It also increased IL-1beta concomitant effect. These findings corresponded to Epitalon effect on diverse stress-induced changes in nSMase activity in cerebral cortex fraction P2. Epitalon activated nSMase in the cerebral cortex membranes of intact mice and increased IL-1beta stimulatory effect on the enzyme activity. The obtained results provided a conclusive evidence of Epitalon stress-protective effect at the level of IL-1beta signal transduction via sphingomyelin pathway in the nerve tissue, as well as at the level of target thymocyte proliferation.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A four-amino-acid peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) derived from pineal gland extracts, given by injection.
explanation.what_it_is: Epithalon is a synthetic peptide — a short chain of four amino acids (the building blocks of proteins) — designed to mimic a naturally occurring pineal peptide. The pineal gland is a tiny endocrine organ in the brain that produces melatonin and regulates circadian rhythm and aging-related processes. Epithalon is typically administered as an injectable compound (research or pharmaceutical, depending on jurisdiction) and is also known as Epitalon or Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly by its amino acid sequence.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Believed to regulate the pineal gland's function and age-related hormonal decline, though human mechanisms remain unproven.
explanation.how_it_works: Epithalon is hypothesized to work by stimulating or restoring the function of the pineal gland — the brain's master regulator of circadian (daily biological) rhythms and several hormones tied to aging. Animal studies suggest it may influence the production of melatonin, a hormone that controls sleep-wake cycles and acts as an antioxidant (a molecule that reduces cellular damage). The peptide is thought to signal to the pineal gland and downstream endocrine organs (particularly the pancreas and reproductive organs) to restore youthful hormone patterns that normally decline with age. However, the exact receptor or signaling pathway by which epithalon achieves this in humans has not been established; most evidence comes from animal models, and the translation to human physiology remains an open question.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term tolerability reported in one human trial; long-term safety, drug interactions, and effects in vulnerable populations are untested.
explanation.safety_detail: The single human study on eye health (an RCT published 2002) did not report serious adverse events over its study duration, though sample size and full adverse event details could not be verified from the abstract. No other human tolerability or safety data were retrieved. Because epithalon is a research-grade peptide often not approved for human use in most countries, long-term safety monitoring in real-world populations is absent.
safety_bullets: Pregnancy and lactation: not studied in humans; unknown safety in these populations.
Renal or hepatic impairment: no trials retrieved; untested in these groups.
Drug interactions: not systematically investigated; unknown whether it interacts with hormone therapies, anticoagulants, or other injectables.
Duration: evidence base consists only of short-term or acute dosing; long-term (months to years) safety is not established.
explanation.chem_meaning: Epithalon is a small, water-loving peptide (XLogP −5.5, meaning it dissolves readily in water and poorly in fats). Its small size and hydrophilic nature mean it does not easily cross cell membranes or the blood-brain barrier without active transport; it must therefore act via surface receptors on cells or after direct injection. This chemistry is typical of peptide hormones and signaling molecules, which usually signal 'from outside' the cell rather than penetrating it.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six animal studies (2003–2008) in rodents and mice found that epithalon reduced spontaneous tumor incidence, slowed carcinogenesis, and modulated tumor cell proliferation and apoptosis (programmed cell death) in the colon and other tissues over lifespan. Studies included both normal aging rodents and genetically predisposed mouse strains (C3H/He, senescence-accelerated mice); some combined epithalon with melatonin. No human trials were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: All evidence is from animal models; no human data exist. Tumor development in mice and rats does not reliably predict cancer outcomes in people, so the grade is capped at Preliminary regardless of animal consistency.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One human RCT (2002) reported that epithalon improved retinal condition in patients with retinitis pigmentosa (a genetic eye disease causing progressive vision loss); however, sample size could not be verified from the abstract, limiting precision. Three animal studies (2002–2003) in rats with hereditary pigmentary dystrophy and age-related retinal changes also found protective or retinoprotective effects. The human and animal findings align directionally, but only one human study exists, so consistency across independent human trials cannot be assessed.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: One small human RCT provides the only direct human evidence; it is encouraging but not large or recent enough to establish efficacy, and animal models do not reliably predict ophthalmic outcomes in humans. Imprecision (unverified sample size) and single-study limitation prevent a higher grade.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two animal studies (2004–2005) in aged primates (monkeys) and rodents found that epithalon restored age-related declines in circulating hormones, including testosterone and pancreatic hormones, and partially normalized pineal and pancreatic function. No human trials on hormone levels or testosterone were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence is animal-only, from primate and rodent models of aging. Hormone dynamics differ substantially between primates/rodents and humans, so even a primate study does not reliably predict human endocrine outcomes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three animal studies (2002–2008) in hypophysectomized (surgically pituitary-removed) and aged chickens and young rodent models found that epithalon enhanced immune cell proliferation (thymocyte blast transformation), modulated interleukin-1β signaling (a key immune messenger), and improved hemostasis (blood clotting) markers. No human immune trials were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: All evidence is from avian (chicken) and small-animal models; immune response in birds and rodents does not reliably translate to human immunology. No human data exist.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base for epithalon consists almost entirely of animal studies conducted primarily in Russia from 2002 to 2008. Only one human trial (an RCT on eye health, 2002) was retrieved; it is relatively old and lacks clearly reported sample sizes and full adverse event details. The animal data cover multiple outcomes (cancer, vision, hormones, immunity) in rodents, mice, and one primate species, but the diversity of animal models and absence of independent human replication mean confidence in human efficacy is low. Most studies predate 2010, and no recent large-scale human trials appear in the retrieved records.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided show a gap: epithalon has been tested in only one human study (eye disease), meaning efficacy in other domains (cancer prevention, hormone restoration, immune function) has never been assessed in people. That single human trial is small and lacks reported sample-size details, precluding firm conclusions even for vision. The animal models span rodents, mice, chickens, and one primate study, but consistency between species is mixed, and whether any animal result will translate to human disease is unknown. Long-term safety (beyond the short observation windows in animal studies) and effects in human subgroups (elderly, those with kidney or liver disease, pregnant individuals) have not been examined. Note: this summary reflects only the ~40 records provided; absence from these records does not mean the broader literature is sparse.

appraisal.headline: All evidence is either animal-only or consists of a single small human study from 2002; no clinical efficacy in humans has been demonstrated for any claimed benefit.

concerns.issue: Zero human evidence for most outcomes
concerns.detail: Cancer/tumor growth (12 studies), testosterone/hormones (2 studies), and immune function (3 studies) are supported entirely by animal models with no human trials. The engine explicitly flags animal-to-human translation as unreliable. Animal models of aging and carcinogenesis are notoriously poor predictors of human pharmacology, and peptide bioavailability differs drastically between rodents and humans.

concerns.issue: Single human study for vision; no replication
concerns.detail: Eye/vision—the only outcome with any human data—rests on one 2002 RCT on retinitis pigmentosa. The engine notes sample size could not be extracted from the abstract, so precision is unconfirmed. Without independent replication in humans, this cannot establish a reliable signal, and the failure to report extractable sample size raises concerns about adequacy of reporting.

All 24 retrieved studies are 15+ years old, clustered in the early 2000s. No recent human trials, mechanistic studies, or dose-optimization work is visible in this sample. This raises the question of whether the research was abandoned, whether modern standards would replicate findings, and whether any regulatory development occurred.

concerns.issue: Sample sizes not extractable; precision unknown
concerns.detail: The engine notes that sample sizes 'could not be extracted' from abstracts across all outcomes. This is unusual and suggests either unusually poor abstract quality, missing numeric data, or summaries too brief to judge statistical power. Small animal studies (common in aging research) can show large effects by chance; without knowing whether studies had n=5 or n=50 per group, effect reliability cannot be assessed.

concerns.issue: No pooled meta-analytic effect reported; heterogeneity unknown
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes, pooled effects are marked 'not extractable.' This prevents assessment of direction consistency, magnitude, or heterogeneity. The cancer outcome lists 12 animal studies spanning different tumor types (mammary, colon, spontaneous) and models (transgenic, induced) without indication whether findings converge or conflict.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanism—pineal peptide regulation of aging and tumor suppression—is plausible at the cellular level (as shown in animal studies of apoptosis and proliferation markers), but a large inferential leap exists between rodent pineal physiology and human cancer prevention. Pineal function, circadian regulation, and age-related carcinogenesis differ substantially between species. The vision outcome (retinitis pigmentosa) has no clear mechanistic bridge from pineal peptide to photoreceptor protection in the abstracts provided. No human pharmacokinetic or target engagement data are visible in these records.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A well-informed skeptic would note that all robust animal tumor models have failed to translate to human cancer prevention—the history of gerontology is littered with compounds that extend lifespan in rodents but show no benefit in humans. The single human vision study is from 2002, never replicated, with unreported sample size; it could easily be a false positive from a small, unblinded, or selectively reported trial. The absence of any human studies on cancer, hormones, or immunity, combined with the commercial gray-market status and regulatory non-approval, suggests either failure to move to clinical testing or that clinical results were negative and unpublished.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A pre-registered, adequately powered RCT (n≥100 per arm) in humans on a clinically meaningful endpoint (e.g., cancer incidence in an at-risk population, or vision loss progression in retinitis pigmentosa patients, with >2-year follow-up) with results published in a peer-reviewed journal would be necessary. Ideally, two independent trials showing consistent benefit would establish human efficacy; mechanistic studies of peptide pharmacokinetics and target binding in humans would strengthen the biological case.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido de cuatro aminoácidos (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) derivado de extractos de la glándula pineal, administrado por inyección.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Epithalón es un péptido sintético — una cadena corta de cuatro aminoácidos (los componentes básicos de las proteínas) — diseñado para imitar un péptido pineal que ocurre naturalmente. La glándula pineal es un pequeño órgano endocrino en el cerebro que produce melatonina y regula el ritmo circadiano y los procesos relacionados con el envejecimiento. Epithalón se administra típicamente como un compuesto inyectable (de investigación o farmacéutico, según la jurisdicción) y también se conoce como Epitalón o Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly por su secuencia de aminoácidos.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Se cree que regula la función de la glándula pineal y el declive hormonal relacionado con la edad, aunque los mecanismos en humanos siguen siendo no probados.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Se hipotetiza que epithalón funciona estimulando o restaurando la función de la glándula pineal — el regulador maestro del cerebro de los ritmos circadianos (biológicos diarios) y varias hormonas vinculadas al envejecimiento. Los estudios en animales sugieren que podría influir en la producción de melatonina, una hormona que controla los ciclos sueño-vigilia y actúa como antioxidante (una molécula que reduce el daño celular). Se cree que el péptido envía señales a la glándula pineal y a órganos endocrinos posteriores (particularmente el páncreas y órganos reproductivos) para restaurar patrones hormonales juveniles que normalmente declina con la edad. Sin embargo, el receptor exacto o la vía de señalización por la cual epithalón logra esto en humanos no ha sido establecido; la mayoría de la evidencia proviene de modelos animales, y la traducción a la fisiología humana sigue siendo una pregunta abierta.
explanation_es.safety_line: Tolerabilidad a corto plazo reportada en un ensayo humano; la seguridad a largo plazo, las interacciones farmacológicas y los efectos en poblaciones vulnerables no han sido probados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: El único estudio humano sobre salud ocular (un ECA publicado en 2002) no reportó eventos adversos graves durante su duración, aunque el tamaño de la muestra y los detalles completos de eventos adversos no pudieron ser verificados del resumen. No se recuperaron otros datos de tolerabilidad o seguridad en humanos. Debido a que epithalón es un péptido de grado de investigación frecuentemente no aprobado para uso humano en la mayoría de los países, el monitoreo de seguridad a largo plazo en poblaciones del mundo real está ausente.
safety_bullets: Embarazo y lactancia: no estudiado en humanos; seguridad desconocida en estas poblaciones.
Insuficiencia renal o hepática: sin ensayos recuperados; no probado en estos grupos.
Interacciones farmacológicas: no investigadas sistemáticamente; se desconoce si interactúa con terapias hormonales, anticoagulantes u otros inyectables.
Duración: la base de evidencia consiste únicamente en dosificación a corto plazo o aguda; la seguridad a largo plazo (meses a años) no está establecida.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Epithalón es un pequeño péptido hidrófilo (XLogP −5.5, lo que significa que se disuelve fácilmente en agua y pobremente en grasas). Su pequeño tamaño y naturaleza hidrófila significa que no cruza fácilmente las membranas celulares o la barrera hematoencefálica sin transporte activo; por lo tanto, debe actuar a través de receptores de superficie en células o después de inyección directa. Esta química es típica de las hormonas peptídicas y moléculas de señalización, que generalmente señalan 'desde afuera' de la célula en lugar de penetrarla.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis estudios en animales (2003–2008) en roedores y ratones encontraron que epithalón redujo la incidencia de tumores espontáneos, ralentizó la carcinogénesis y moduló la proliferación y apoptosis (muerte celular programada) de células tumorales en el colon y otros tejidos durante la vida útil. Los estudios incluyeron tanto roedores de envejecimiento normal como cepas de ratones genéticamente predispuestos (C3H/He, ratones con envejecimiento acelerado); algunos combinaron epithalón con melatonina. No se recuperaron ensayos humanos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Toda la evidencia proviene de modelos animales; no existen datos humanos. El desarrollo de tumores en ratones y ratas no predice de manera confiable los resultados del cáncer en personas, por lo que la clasificación se limita a Preliminar independientemente de la consistencia animal.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ECA humano (2002) reportó que epithalón mejoró la condición retiniana en pacientes con retinitis pigmentosa (una enfermedad ocular genética que causa pérdida progresiva de visión); sin embargo, el tamaño de la muestra no pudo ser verificado del resumen, limitando la precisión. Tres estudios en animales (2002–2003) en ratas con distrofia pigmentaria hereditaria y cambios retinianos relacionados con la edad también encontraron efectos protectores o retinioprotectores. Los hallazgos humanos y animales se alinean direccionalmente, pero solo existe un estudio humano, por lo que la consistencia entre ensayos humanos independientes no puede ser evaluada.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Un pequeño ECA humano proporciona la única evidencia humana directa; es alentador pero no es lo suficientemente grande o reciente como para establecer eficacia, y los modelos animales no predicen de manera confiable los resultados oftalmológicos en humanos. La imprecisión (tamaño de muestra no verificado) y la limitación de un solo estudio impiden una clasificación más alta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios en animales (2004–2005) en primates envejecidos (monos) y roedores encontraron que epithalón restauró los declives relacionados con la edad en las hormonas circulantes, incluida la testosterona y las hormonas pancreáticas, y normalizó parcialmente la función pineal y pancreática. No se recuperaron ensayos humanos sobre niveles hormonales o testosterona.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia es solo en animales, de modelos de envejecimiento en primates y roedores. La dinámica hormonal difiere sustancialmente entre primates/roedores y humanos, por lo que incluso un estudio en primates no predice de manera confiable los resultados endocrinos humanos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres estudios en animales (2002–2008) en gallinas hipofisectomizadas (cirugía de glándula pituitaria extirpada) y modelos jóvenes de roedores con envejecimiento encontraron que epithalón mejoró la proliferación de células inmunológicas (transformación de blastos de timocitos), moduló la señalización de interleucina-1β (un mensajero inmunológico clave) y mejoró los marcadores de hemostasia (coagulación sanguínea). No se recuperaron ensayos inmunológicos humanos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Toda la evidencia proviene de modelos aviares (gallina) y de pequeños animales; la respuesta inmunológica en aves y roedores no se traduce de manera confiable a la inmunología humana. No existen datos humanos.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia para epithalón consiste casi enteramente en estudios en animales realizados principalmente en Rusia de 2002 a 2008. Solo se recuperó un ensayo humano (un ECA sobre salud ocular, 2002); es relativamente antiguo y carece de tamaños de muestra claramente reportados y detalles completos de eventos adversos. Los datos animales cubren múltiples resultados (cáncer, visión, hormonas, inmunidad) en roedores, ratones y una especie de primate, pero la diversidad de modelos animales y la ausencia de replicación humana independiente significan que la confianza en la eficacia humana es baja. La mayoría de los estudios son anteriores a 2010, y no aparecen ensayos humanos grandes recientes en los registros recuperados.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran una brecha: epithalón ha sido probado en solo un estudio humano (enfermedad ocular), lo que significa que la eficacia en otros dominios (prevención del cáncer, restauración hormonal, función inmunológica) nunca ha sido evaluada en personas. Ese único ensayo humano es pequeño y carece de detalles de tamaño de muestra reportado, lo que impide conclusiones firmes incluso para la visión. Los modelos animales abarcan roedores, ratones, gallinas y un estudio de primate, pero la consistencia entre especies es mixta, y si algún resultado animal se traducirá a la enfermedad humana es desconocido. La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de las ventanas de observación corta en estudios animales) y los efectos en subgrupos humanos (ancianos, aquellos con enfermedad renal o hepática, individuos embarazadas) no han sido examinados. Nota: este resumen refleja solo los ~40 registros proporcionados; la ausencia de estos registros no significa que la literatura más amplia sea escasa.

appraisal_es.headline: Toda la evidencia es únicamente en animales o consiste en un único estudio humano pequeño de 2002; no se ha demostrado eficacia clínica en humanos para ningún beneficio reclamado.

concerns.issue: Cero evidencia humana para la mayoría de los resultados
concerns.detail: Crecimiento de cáncer/tumores (12 estudios), testosterona/hormonas (2 estudios) e inmunidad (3 estudios) se sustentan enteramente en modelos animales sin ensayos humanos. El motor explícitamente señala la traducción animal-a-humano como no confiable. Los modelos animales de envejecimiento y carcinogénesis son notoriamente malos predictores de farmacología humana, y la biodisponibilidad de péptidos difiere drásticamente entre roedores y humanos.

concerns.issue: Único estudio humano para visión; sin replicación
concerns.detail: Ojo/visión—el único resultado con datos humanos—se basa en un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2002 sobre retinitis pigmentosa. El motor señala que el tamaño de la muestra no pudo ser extraído del resumen, por lo que la precisión es inconfirmada. Sin replicación independiente en humanos, esto no puede establecer una señal confiable, y la falta de reportar un tamaño de muestra extraíble genera preocupaciones sobre la adecuación de la presentación de datos.

Los 24 estudios recuperados tienen más de 15 años, agrupados en principios de los 2000. No hay ensayos humanos recientes, estudios mecanísticos o trabajo de optimización de dosis visible en esta muestra. Esto plantea la pregunta de si la investigación fue abandonada, si los estándares modernos replicarían los hallazgos, y si ocurrió algún desarrollo regulatorio.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de muestra no extraíbles; precisión desconocida
concerns.detail: El motor señala que los tamaños de muestra 'no pudieron ser extraídos' de resúmenes en todos los resultados. Esto es inusual y sugiere calidad de resumen inusualmente pobre, datos numéricos faltantes, o sumarios demasiado breves para juzgar poder estadístico. Los estudios animales pequeños (comunes en investigación de envejecimiento) pueden mostrar efectos grandes por azar; sin saber si los estudios tenían n=5 o n=50 por grupo, la confiabilidad del efecto no puede ser evaluada.

concerns.issue: Sin efecto combinado de metanálisis reportado; heterogeneidad desconocida
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados, los efectos combinados están marcados como 'no extraíbles'. Esto impide evaluar consistencia de dirección, magnitud o heterogeneidad. El resultado de cáncer lista 12 estudios animales abarcando diferentes tipos de tumor (mamario, colon, espontáneo) y modelos (transgénico, inducido) sin indicación de si los hallazgos convergen o divergen.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo propuesto—regulación de péptido pineal del envejecimiento y supresión tumoral—es plausible a nivel celular (como se muestra en estudios animales de marcadores de apoptosis y proliferación), pero existe un gran salto inferencial entre la fisiología pineal de roedores y la prevención del cáncer humano. La función pineal, regulación circadiana y carcinogénesis relacionada con la edad difieren sustancialmente entre especies. El resultado de visión (retinitis pigmentosa) no tiene un puente mecanístico claro desde el péptido pineal hasta la protección del fotorreceptor en los resúmenes proporcionados. No hay datos de farmacocinética humana o compromiso del objetivo visibles en estos registros.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico bien informado señalaría que todos los modelos robustos de tumores animales han fallado en traducirse a prevención del cáncer humano—la historia de la gerontología está llena de compuestos que extienden la vida en roedores pero no muestran beneficio en humanos. El único estudio humano de visión es de 2002, nunca replicado, con tamaño de muestra no reportado; podría fácilmente ser un falso positivo de un ensayo pequeño, no cegado, o selectivamente reportado. La ausencia de cualquier estudio humano sobre cáncer, hormonas o inmunidad, combinada con el estado comercial de mercado gris y no aprobación regulatoria, sugiere bien falta de avance a ensayos clínicos o que los resultados clínicos fueron negativos e no publicados.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado preregistrado y adecuadamente potenciado (n≥100 por grupo) en humanos sobre un resultado clínicamente significativo (p. ej., incidencia de cáncer en una población en riesgo, o progresión de pérdida de visión en pacientes con retinitis pigmentosa, con seguimiento >2 años) con resultados publicados en una revista revisada por pares sería necesario. Idealmente, dos ensayos independientes mostrando beneficio consistente establecería eficacia humana; estudios mecanísticos de farmacocinética de péptidos y unión al objetivo en humanos fortalecerían el caso biológico.
